- **Two-sum headline:** *50 satisfied / 51 engineering-closed of 62 boilerplate rows; the remaining 11 are honestly `PARTIAL` and routed to named open homes* (P38.2 ×2, P37.66, P35.2 ×2, P35.4, P37.3, P38.3a, BL-089, BL-051, BL-082).
- Every open verdict routes to a live home per ADR-150; the once-bare family now carries zero unparameterised `MET-DIFFERENTLY` rows.

## 4. `SIG-UI-040` — the named addition

SEED-15 had already withdrawn `SIG-UI-040`'s parameterised verdict to bare `MET-DIFFERENTLY` because neither ADR-108 nor ADR-133 names the id (ADR-150 D1/D4; landed ADR bodies are frozen). C2 wrote **ADR-200 — *Search without a dedicated engine*** (`docs/adr/ADR-200-search-without-a-dedicated-engine.md`): it names `SIG-UI-040`, records the alternative (bounded `pg_trgm` `/v1/search` per ADR-108; per-compartment SQLite FTS5 release artifacts per ADR-133; no dedicated engine by design), and keeps the dedicated-engine option trigger-gated with the licensing check the SHOULD names (home BL-084). Final verdict `MET-DIFFERENTLY(ADR-200)`; assessment `SIG-UI-040:r11-3` supersedes `r11-2`.

## 5. Comparison with F2b's sample estimate (labelled comparison, not a target)

F2b's 13-row sample of this family estimated **≈ 54 % not met** among the boilerplate rows. The full 62-row re-verdict lands materially better — **11 of 62 (≈ 18 %) PARTIAL, 0 MISSING** — while still finding real incompleteness the bulk acceptance had concealed (e.g. `SIG-ENG-037`'s missing regression check, `SIG-CHART-006`/`021`'s public-surface gaps, `SIG-ENG-022`/`023`/`025`'s hosted/ops gaps). The sample was directionally right that the blanket verdict concealed unmet requirements; it overstated the share, which is exactly why the re-verdict was done row-by-row rather than extrapolated.
